html:
After World War II hundreds of thousands of Puerto Ricans moved to the mainland United States, above all to New York City, in what is called the Great Migration. As US citizens they could move freely.

Cheap flights, jobs in the garment trade and the loss of farm work under Operation Bootstrap drove the move. By the 1970s Puerto Ricans filled East Harlem, called El Barrio, and parts of the Bronx and Brooklyn.

They built a Nuyorican culture with its own poetry, salsa music and politics, and faced poverty and discrimination. Today more Puerto Ricans live on the mainland than on the island, a trend sped up by the debt crisis and Hurricane Maria.
